sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Hempfield, PA?
sections.html:
Selling in Hempfield is simpler on paperwork than in many Pennsylvania municipalities, because the township does not require a certificate of occupancy for a home sale. What you do need is a clear picture of the septic or sewer situation, the 2 percent transfer tax split, and the county assessment record.

Hempfield is a township in Westmoreland County, and it is big. It covers about 77 square miles, and Wikipedia describes it as the largest suburb in the Pittsburgh metropolitan area by population. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 41,421 residents, which is down 0.2 percent from the April 2020 base, so the township is stable rather than booming, and sellers compete mostly with other established single-family homes.

Owners here choose between an agent listing, a sale by owner and a direct cash purchase. All three finish the same way, with a deed recorded at the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg and the transfer tax paid at that office.

sections.h2: Where is Hempfield and what is inside it?
sections.html:
The city of Greensburg and six boroughs sit entirely inside the township: Southwest Greensburg, South Greensburg, Youngwood, New Stanton, Arona and Adamsburg. Hempfield was incorporated on April 6, 1773, and takes its name from the hemp fields of the older Hempfield in Lancaster County.

Named communities within the township include Fort Allen, Grapeville, Hannastown, Carbon, Radebaugh, Maplewood Terrace, West Point and Luxor. Neighbors include Salem, Unity, Mount Pleasant, East Huntingdon, South Huntingdon, Sewickley and North Huntingdon townships, plus the city of Jeannette. The township is large enough that a home near Greensburg and a rural parcel miles away can have very different values.

  • Schools: the Hempfield Area School District, which also serves Adamsburg, Armbrust, Bovard, Grapeville, Hunker, Luxor, Manor, New Stanton and Youngwood.
  • Higher education: the University of Pittsburgh at Greensburg, the Youngwood campus of Westmoreland County Community College, and a Carlow University satellite campus.
  • Policing: the township relies on the Pennsylvania State Police as its sole law enforcement agency.

sections.h2: What shapes the Hempfield economy and home demand?
sections.html:
Hempfield is the retail hub for Westmoreland County and the Laurel Highlands. U.S. Route 30 passes the Westmoreland Mall and the adjoining Live! Casino Pittsburgh, and Greengate Centre is the area's largest big-box center. Light industry operates from several industrial parks, including RIDC Westmoreland, which straddles the Hempfield and East Huntingdon line.

The 2011 tornado is part of local memory. An EF2 tornado touched down on March 23, 2011 southwest of Greensburg and damaged scores of homes in the West Hempfield area and the Fort Allen neighborhood, along with Hempfield Area High School and Harrold Middle School. A buyer may ask whether a house in those areas needed storm repairs.

The age profile also matters for demand. The Census Bureau reports that 26.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 84.7 percent of housing units are owner occupied. That mix produces many estate sales and downsizing moves.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Hempfield homes?
sections.html:
Hempfield homes are owner occupied, moderately priced and held for a long time. More than nine in ten residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

A typical seller here is not racing a mortgage payment. More often the house is a long-held family home, an inherited property, or a house that needs work the owner no longer wants to manage.

sections.h2: What local rules apply when a Hempfield house sells?
sections.html:
The township's planning and code department says a certificate of occupancy is not required to sell a home. Two other checks apply depending on how the house drains.

  • On-lot septic. Contact the township's Sewage Enforcement Officer about any dye test the buyer or lender wants.
  • Public sewer. Call the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County at 724-755-5800 for the sewer account and any test or final reading.
  • Permits. Open permits or unpermitted work should be sorted out first. The township says zoning permits take up to 15 business days and building permits up to 30.

The code office is at 1132 Woodward Drive, Suite A, and answers at 724-834-7232. The county assessment office, at 724-830-3409, can explain whether a building permit changes the assessed value. Landlord and tenant disputes go to the Pennsylvania Attorney General's consumer hotline, which the township lists at 1-800-441-2555.

Township property tax is low in dollar terms. The township levies 3 mills for general purposes and 3 mills for a dedicated fire service tax, so a $25,000 assessed value pays $150 a year to the township. School and county taxes are separate and larger. Areas inside a street light district also pay a yearly light district assessment.

sections.h2: How is the transfer tax split in Hempfield?
sections.html:
Hempfield's total realty transfer tax is 2 percent of the sale value. Pennsylvania takes 1 percent, the township takes 0.5 percent and the Hempfield Area School District takes the final 0.5 percent. It is paid through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds, whose office the township lists at 724-830-3518.

On a house sold at the township's $232,100 median value, that is about $4,642 in total, and the contract decides how the buyer and seller divide it. The state's rules make both parties liable to the recorder, and they list exemptions for certain family transfers and for property passing through inheritance.

Ask the title company to show the transfer tax line before you sign. If you are selling an inherited house, ask whether the exemption for passing by inheritance applies to your deed.

sections.h2: How do Westmoreland County assessment appeals work?
sections.html:
The county Tax Assessment Office handles the values that set every property tax bill in the township. Anyone can appeal a change of assessment within 40 days of the mailing of the notice. An annual appeal must be on file by August 1 of each year and takes effect for the following tax year.

The Board of Assessment Appeals meets on the second Thursday of each month at 9:00 a.m. at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue, Suite 440, in Greensburg. Appeal forms are on the county site or at the assessment office.

If you plan to sell, check the assessed value before listing. A buyer's lender will look at the current tax amount, and an assessment you believe is too high can be appealed by the next August 1.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Hempfield house?
sections.html:
It fits when the house needs work, when it is an estate property, or when you want to set the closing date yourself. It is less useful for a move-in ready home you can list quickly.

Weigh any cash offer against the net from a listing after commission, transfer tax, repairs and the months it takes to find a buyer. To get a cash offer on a Hempfield house in its current condition, you can ask Cash Home Buyers and then compare.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Hempfield house?
faqs.a: No. The Hempfield Township planning and code department states that a certificate of occupancy is not required for the sale of a home.

faqs.q: Who handles a dye test for a Hempfield home sale?
faqs.a: It depends on the system. For a septic system, contact the township's Sewage Enforcement Officer. For public sewer, call the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County at 724-755-5800.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Hempfield sale?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent of the value: 1 percent to Pennsylvania, 0.5 percent to the township and 0.5 percent to the Hempfield Area School District. The Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Hempfield Township?
faqs.a: The Hempfield Area School District. It also covers Adamsburg, Armbrust, Bovard, Grapeville, Hunker, Luxor, Manor, New Stanton and Youngwood.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Westmoreland County assessment?
faqs.a: An annual appeal is due by August 1 and applies to the following tax year. After a change of assessment notice, you have 40 days from the mailing to appeal.
